requirement_text: UNIGE requires foreign secondary diplomas to demonstrate 'formation générale' (general education) across six subject areas: (1) first language, (2) second language, (3) mathematics, (4) natural sciences (biology, chemistry, or physics), (5) social sciences/humanities (geography, history, or economics/law), and (6) a free-choice subject from categories 2, 4, or 5, or informatics, or philosophy.
source_authority_note: unige.ch is University of Geneva's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: A companion PDF ('Conditions d'immatriculation à l'Université de Genève 2026-2027') exists at unige.ch/immatriculations but failed to parse as text via WebFetch (returned corrupted/binary content); this record instead relies on the HTML 'conditions' overview page, which independently states the same six-category structure.
researcher_notes: CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED: this six-subject framework matches the central swissuniversities framework (system file REQ-2026-08-21-0001) essentially verbatim in structure — no conflict found.

requirement_text: CONDITIONAL RECOGNITION (verbatim shape): Germany's Zeugnis der allgemeinen Hochschulreife (Abitur) is recognized with a minimum average of 2.5/5. If that minimum is not achieved, the certificate can still be accepted if the candidate provides 'l'attestation d'admission, dans la filière visée, d'une université reconnue par l'UNIGE en Allemagne' (an admission attestation, in the intended field of study, from a UNIGE-recognized German university) — i.e. recognition is conditional on EITHER the grade average OR an alternative university-admission attestation, not a flat pass/fail threshold alone.
limitations: Sourced from an AI-summarized WebFetch of the HTML overview page (the authoritative PDF failed to parse); recommend re-verification of the exact 2.5/5 figure against a successfully-parsed primary document before treating as final.
researcher_notes: FLAGGED PER COORDINATOR INSTRUCTION: genuine conditional-recognition example (grade threshold OR alternative university-attestation pathway), recorded as the actual 'either/or' condition rather than collapsed into a single number.

requirement_text: CONDITIONAL RECOGNITION (verbatim shape): France's Baccalauréat général is recognized with a minimum average of 12/20. Where that minimum is not achieved, admission can still be obtained if it 'peut être compensée par la réussite de deux années d'études dans une université ... reconnus par l'UNIGE' (can be offset by successfully completing two years of study at a UNIGE-recognized university) — recognition conditional on EITHER the grade average OR two years of prior university study, not a flat single threshold.
limitations: Sourced from AI-summarized WebFetch of the HTML overview page; the authoritative 2026-2027 conditions PDF failed to parse as text. Recommend re-verification against a successfully-parsed primary document.
researcher_notes: Second example of the 'grade-OR-university-study' conditional shape, structurally parallel to the Germany record (REQ-2026-08-21-0402) and to UZH's own §17 partial-recognition-plus-2-years rule (REQ-2026-08-21-0302) — this pattern (numeric threshold OR 2 years of prior university study as an alternative path) recurs across multiple Swiss institutions, suggesting it traces back to a shared swissuniversities-level recommendation, though we did not find this specific 'OR' structure spelled out on the central swissuniversities page itself during this pass.

requirement_text: COMPOUND CONDITIONAL: Hong Kong's HKDSE is recognized with a minimum grade of 3 per subject (or C for category-C languages), PLUS an admission attestation from a UNIGE-recognized Hong Kong university, PLUS the candidate must 'réussir l'examen de français organisé par l'UNIGE' (pass the French exam organized by UNIGE). All three conditions apply together (a compound AND, not an OR alternative like the Germany/France examples).
limitations: Sourced from AI-summarized WebFetch; authoritative PDF failed to parse.
researcher_notes: Included specifically to illustrate that conditional recognition is not always an 'either/or' — some certificates require an 'AND' combination of multiple conditions simultaneously. Recorded as the actual compound structure rather than simplified to one requirement.

requirement_text: International Baccalaureate is recognized with conditions: three Higher Level exams (including one science — mathematics, chemistry, biology, or physics) plus three Standard Level exams; minimum 32 points excluding bonus points; minimum average of 12/20; and the candidate must additionally 'réussir l'examen de français' (pass a French exam) organized by UNIGE.
limitations: The 32-point minimum is notably lower than EPFL's stated 38/42 IB minimum for its own bachelor programs (EPFL file, REQ-2026-08-21-0104) — this is NOT a conflict, since these are two different institutions independently setting their own thresholds atop the same base IB-recognition concept, not the same institution described two different ways. Sourced from AI-summarized WebFetch; authoritative PDF failed to parse — recommend re-verification of exact point figures.

requirement_text: For IB, certain subjects are explicitly excluded from counting toward UNIGE's recognition criteria, including (per the source): 'littérature et représentation théâtrale, politique mondiale, technologie de l'information dans une société globale, histoire de l'islam, psychologie, anthropologie sociale et culturelle' (theatre literature and performance, global politics, information technology in a global society, history of Islam, psychology, social and cultural anthropology), among others.
limitations: This exclusion list is likely not exhaustive as extracted (source text says 'among others' implicitly via truncation) — treat as a representative sample, not the complete list. Recommend fetching the underlying PDF or full page for the complete list before using this as a final eligibility check for a specific student.
researcher_notes: Recorded explicitly as an EXCLUSION clause (subjects that do NOT count) rather than omitted — losing this would make an otherwise-accurate IB requirement record misleadingly permissive.

requirement_text: ECUS (supplementary exam) is required for applicants from a list of countries including Egypt, Ethiopia, Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, and Lebanon, among others, even where other conditions (e.g. a home-country university admission attestation) are separately met: 'Dans le cas où les conditions ci-dessus sont remplies, le/la candidat-e devra également réussir l'ECUS' (where the above conditions are met, the candidate must ALSO pass the ECUS) — i.e. ECUS is an additional, stacked requirement for these countries, not a substitute for the other conditions.
scope: Egypt, Ethiopia, Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Lebanon, and other listed countries
limitations: Country list as extracted is likely partial ('among others' implied); authoritative PDF failed to parse. Recommend re-verification for the complete country list.
researcher_notes: Supplementary-exam-shaped requirement, correctly kept as an ADDITIONAL stacked condition (not a replacement/alternative) per the source's own 'également' (also) wording — flagged so this nuance (stacked vs. alternative) is not lost.

requirement_text: A French language exam organized by UNIGE is required for certain diploma origins including Germany, Italy, Romania, and Albania, among others; exemptions ('dispenses') are possible under conditions not fully enumerated in the source extracted.
scope: Germany, Italy, Romania, Albania, and other listed countries

requirement_text: As a fallback admission pathway, UNIGE recognizes 'un premier diplôme universitaire ... exigé ... au terme d'une formation d'une durée de 3 ans minimum (au moins 180 crédits ECTS)' (a first university degree, from a UNIGE-recognized institution, of minimum 3-year duration with at least 180 ECTS credits) as an alternative basis for admission, independent of the secondary-school-certificate pathway.

program_name: Bachelor in Information Systems and Business Analytics (GSEM)
requirement_text: A new Bachelor program in Information Systems & Business Analytics at the Geneva School of Economics and Management (GSEM) has a special one-off application window for the 2026-2027 cycle: '6 juillet au 15 août 2026' (July 6 to August 15, 2026). The source explicitly scopes this: 'Cette dérogation vaut uniquement pour les candidat-es qui s'inscrivent pour le Baccalauréat universitaire (Bachelor) en systèmes d'information et business analytics' (this derogation applies only to candidates registering for this specific Bachelor program).
limitations: Deliberately NOT generalized to other UNIGE programs — recorded with program_name scoped explicitly since the source itself stresses this is a one-program exception.

requirement_text: UNIGE does NOT apply a numerus clausus or the EMS test at first-year entry to the Bachelor in Human Medicine. Progression from 1st to 2nd year instead happens via a competitive exam ('concours'), introduced starting 2017-2018: 'Dès 2017-2018, conformément à l'article 17 (5) de la Loi sur l'Université, le Rectorat a autorisé l'instauration d'un concours pour le passage de la 1ère à la 2ème année' (as of 2017-2018, per Article 17(5) of the University Law, the Rectorate authorized a competitive exam for progression from 1st to 2nd year). First-year assessment comprises three partial evaluations (ESMS, ESFO, ESMB); passing requires a score ≥4.0, but passing alone does not guarantee 2nd-year admission — ranking against available capacity decides. Students scoring 3.0–3.75, or who pass without being admitted, may retake the exam once.
source_authority_note: unige.ch official Faculty of Medicine domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: This page focuses on the 1st-year exam structure and 2nd-year progression; it does not itself state UNIGE's foreign-qualification requirements for FIRST-year entry to medicine (those follow UNIGE's general bachelor admission rules recorded above in this file — no medicine-specific foreign-qualification variant was found).
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT SHAPE DISTINCTION (per task brief and coordinator note): this is categorically different from ETH Zurich's and UZH's EMS-gated entry. Recorded as its own entrance_exam-shaped requirement (a 2nd-year competitive exam) rather than forced into the EMS mold. See Switzerland-system file record REQ-2026-08-21-0010 for the cross-institutional summary of this distinction.
